article_title: ICE agents should be deployed during midterms—Trump ally
article_content:
Steve Bannon, a former White House strategist and close ally of Trump, suggested the deployment of ICE to airports could be used as a "test run" for the agency’s potential role during the 2026 midterm elections.
Bannon was speaking amid an ongoing partial federal government shutdown that has left many Transportation Security Administration (TSA) officers working without pay and sparked staffing challenges at major airports. In response, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) authorised ICE personnel to assist in some airport operations, such as managing crowd movement and checking identification
“We can use this as a test run, as a test case, to really perfect ICE’s involvement in the 2026 midterms,” Bannon said on his War Room podcast Monday during a conversation with conservative commentator Mike Davis.
Davis endorsed the idea of deploying federal immigration agents to polling places in the upcoming November midterms.
“I think we should have ICE agents at the polling place because if you’re an illegal alien, you can’t vote," Davis told Bannon.
“It’s against the law. It’s a federal crime for you to vote in federal elections. And so if you’re an American citizen, you should be happy that ICE is there, because you’re not going to have illegal aliens cancelling out your vote,” Davis added.
Why It Matters
Advocates of stricter election enforcement argue that illegal voting by non‑citizens is a legitimate concern, though multiple studies and election officials have found instances of such voting to be rare. Critics, including civil rights groups argue that placing armed federal agents at polling locations risks violating long‑standing legal norms against voter intimidation and could deter turnout among eligible voters.
The White House refused to rule out deploying ICE agents to polling sites this November, with Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt saying she could offer “no guarantee” they won’t be present.
What To Know
DHS has repeatedly maintained that ICE agents will not be stationed at polling locations for the upcoming elections.
A spokesperson for DHS previously told Newsweek: "ILLEGAL ALIENS SHOULD NEVER BE ALLOWED TO VOTE IN AMERICAN ELECTIONS. Only Americans citizens should be electing American leaders."
The President urged Congress to pass the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) Act, legislation that would require voters nationwide to provide proof of citizenship and photo identification, among other changes.
Republican lawmakers continue to push for stricter voting requirements, arguing that tighter rules are needed to prevent illegal voting, including by undocumented immigrants, a practice that studies show is extremely rare. The bill, officially called the Secure and Accessible Voting Elections (SAVE) Act by some GOP sponsors, reflects ongoing partisan debates over election security and voter access.
House Democrats have proposed legislation to bar ICE agents from polling places during the 2026 midterm elections.
Rep. April McClain Delaney of Maryland announced in a press release on March 2 that she will introduce the Democracy Without Intimidation Act, a bill aimed at preventing federal law enforcement officers from showing up at polling places. The bill would close that gap by making it a crime for senior officials in federal law enforcement agencies to order officers or agents to operate at polling locations, with penalties of up to five years in prison or a fine and a five-year statute of limitations.
Similar legislation, the Stop ICE Election Militarization Act, has been introduced by Reps. John B. Larson of Connecticut, Nikema Williams of Georgia, and Veronica Escobar of Texas. The bill would criminalize interference at polling places and restrict immigration enforcement in the four weeks leading up to federal elections, except in cases with individualized probable cause or imminent threat.
ICE and Customs and Border Protection have been thrust into the forefront of the national conversation surrounding immigration enforcement as the Trump administration launched a large-scale mass deportation program. The agencies, which fall under the umbrella of the Department of Homeland Security, have faced a litany of allegations of excessive use of force and aggressive tactics, including multiple fatal shootings during federal operations.
In Minneapolis, Minnesota, Renée Nicole Good, a mother of three and poet, was shot and killed by an ICE agent in January during a federal enforcement action, an incident that sparked nationwide protests. Weeks later, two CBP agents shot and killed ICU nurse Alex Pretti. In February, Newsweek revealed that an ICE agent shot and killed Ruben Ray Martinez in Texas in 2025, a fact that was not disclosed publicly for nearly a year.
What People Are Saying
Congresswoman Veronica Escobar of Texas said in a press release: “Donald Trump and his administration have made clear their intention to interfere with the midterms."
A DHS official previously told Newsweek: "ICE is not planning operations targeting polling locations. ICE conducts intelligence-driven targeted enforcement, and if an active public safety threat endangered a polling location, they may be arrested as a result of that targeted enforcement action."
Steve Bannon, a former White House adviser, said on his War Room podcast in February: "You're damn right we're gonna have ICE surround the polls come November. We're not gonna sit here and allow you to steal the country again. And you can whine and cry and throw your toys out of the pram all you want, but we will never again allow an election to be stolen."
What Happens Next
The midterms will take place in November.
